name: Health and Wellbeing
description: A careful evidence-synthesis blueprint for health, wellness, behavior, care delivery, and quality of life.

guidance: Define population, setting, exposure or intervention, comparator, outcome, follow-up period, and evidence type where available.
Separate source-reported claims, observed association, clinical significance, statistical uncertainty, lived experience, and causal evidence.
Organize analysis around burden or context, outcomes, contributing factors, care or intervention pathways, equity, and evidence quality.
Preserve denominators, absolute and relative effects, baseline risk, units, time horizon, and adverse outcomes in comparisons.
Do not provide diagnosis or treatment instruction beyond the source; surface uncertainty, contraindications, and applicability limits.
Use charts only for comparable populations and outcome definitions; never visualize isolated percentages without denominator context.
Recommendations must be framed as evidence-supported considerations, not individualized medical advice.

sections.title: Health Context and Evidence-Supported Answer
sections.purpose: Define the health question and population, then answer the objective at the level justified by the evidence.

blocks.title: Population and Evidence Profile
instructions: State population, setting, intervention or exposure, comparator, outcomes, follow-up, evidence type, and material missing context when available.

blocks.title: Evidence-Supported Summary
instructions: Answer the objective with the principal outcome, magnitude or direction, applicability, important harm or trade-off, and uncertainty.
Do not imply diagnosis, individualized treatment, or causality beyond the source design.

blocks.title: Health and Wellbeing Findings
instructions: Present distinct findings about population, outcomes, determinants, experience, care, equity, benefits, harms, or uncertainty with denominators and locations where available.

sections.title: Outcomes, Determinants and Lived Context
sections.purpose: Explain the observed health or wellbeing pattern and the evidenced factors associated with differences in outcome.

blocks.title: Outcome and Determinant Analysis
instructions: Analyze outcomes, symptoms, function, quality of life, behavior, access, social context, and heterogeneity only where evidenced.
Separate association, reported experience, and causal inference.

blocks.title: Care or Influence Pathway
instructions: Map one supported pathway from need or exposure through access, intervention, behavior, or mechanism to outcome; label uncertain links.

sections.title: Intervention, Access and Equity
sections.purpose: Assess whom an intervention or care model reaches, what outcomes are observed, and where benefits, burdens, or access differ.

blocks.title: Benefits, Harms and Applicability
instructions: Compare benefit, harm, burden, feasibility, access, and subgroup applicability using absolute quantities and time horizons when available.
Do not generalize beyond studied or described populations.

blocks.title: Comparable Outcome Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one health claim with comparable outcome, access, burden, or subgroup evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative health evidence is available.

instructions: Require compatible outcome definitions, populations, denominators, units, and follow-up; show uncertainty when supplied and avoid causal visual framing for observational evidence.

sections.title: Evidence Basis and Practical Considerations
sections.purpose: Make the source basis auditable and identify evidence-supported considerations without giving individualized medical advice.

blocks.title: Clinical and Lived-Evidence Trail
instructions: Tie findings to population, outcome definition, effect or account, timeframe, study or source context, and location.

blocks.title: Evidence-Supported Considerations
instructions: Frame considerations for policy, service design, research, or informed discussion with prerequisites and monitoring signals.

sections.title: Uncertainty, Safety and Evidence Limits
sections.purpose: State limitations that constrain interpretation, safety, applicability, equity, or causal conclusions.

blocks.title: Limitations and Safety Caveats
instructions: Identify missing denominators, comparator, baseline risk, confounding control, uncertainty, harms, follow-up, subgroup representation, outcome validity, or implementation context only when material.
